newsitem.title: THAILAND: At least 63 killed in Thai resort hotel fire.
newsitem.headline: At least 63 killed in Thai resort hotel fire.

text.p: At least 63 people including five Westerners were killed in a hotel fire in this Thai resort town on Friday, and the final number could go as high as 100, police said. They said 43 of the charred bodies at the 16-storey, 400-room Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel had been identified by police, who said most of the victims were Thai. Three men and two women were Westerners of unknown nationality, they said.

Sixty-five people were injured in the fire. Government officials blamed a lack of sprinklers and locked fire exits for the high death toll from the blaze which broke out in the ground floor coffee shop of the hotel around 8:30 a.m. (0130 GMT) and then spread from the sixth floor to the 12th floor of the building.

Heavy smoke was still coming from the building hours after the fire began and police said firefighters were finding bodies in almost every room they opened. Bodies have been difficult to identify because they were badly charred, police said.

More than 300 people, mostly Thais attending seminars, were in the hotel at the time the fire started. Rescue workers said most of the seminar participants ran downstairs from the fifth and sixth floor where the seminars were being held to escape the fire, but got trapped between burning levels. Police said this was Thailand's worst-ever hotel fire.
